title: Photokeratitis: If Your Eyes
Start Burning and Feel Sandy
Hours After a Sunny Day Outside
3 Habits Behind UV Eye Damage

items.name: What photokeratitis actually is
body: pain often hits in the middle
of the night after a sunny day

items.name: Hours outside without wraparound sunglasses
body: on the water, or on snow
reflect UV back into your eyes,
faster than it feels like it should

items.name: Grab real UV sunglasses first
body: Put them on before you head out —

items.name: Tanning beds and welding arcs count too
body: or a quick glance at a welding arc
as a full afternoon at the beach

items.name: Rubbing your eyes instead of treating them
body: your eyes get a break from light

items.name: Rest, don't rub, when it flares up
body: Skip contact lenses until the pain

headline: Wraparound UV sunglasses outdoors,
and real UV protection near
tanning lamps or welding arcs
plus a dark, tear-supported break
when it flares up —
these habits stop repeat damage
tip: Grab sunglasses labeled 100% UV protection or UV400 before heading out, and use protective UV goggles anywhere tanning lamps or welding arcs are running
If it flares up, rest in a dim room with preservative-free artificial tears and skip contacts until the pain and light sensitivity are fully gone
